useCase.summary: AI sales assistant that queries and creates CRM records in a customer's Salesforce org via SOQL queries and record creation.

verdict.headline: Connect today with Composio's managed OAuth app. For production in a customer org, register your own External Client App; no provider review is needed unless you list on AgentExchange, but the org admin must approve the app.
verdict.startToday: Start the managed Composio connection now (minutes), and ask the customer's Salesforce org admin to approve or install the app early: that wait is outside your control. Then create your own External Client App in Setup > App Manager; Connected Apps may no longer be creatable (reported, low confidence).

composio.why: Composio offers a managed OAUTH2 app for Salesforce, so you can connect in minutes. For production, an own External Client App gives you control over refresh-token policies (idle TTL, IP allowlist) and your own branding. Creating one is self-serve and needs no provider review for your own use.

neededFor: Long-lived offline access so the assistant can refresh tokens without re-prompting the user
Not needed for this use case; skip it

requirements.item: A Salesforce org where you can create External Client Apps (Setup access to App Manager)
A Composio project to hold the auth config (managed or custom OAuth2 credentials)
Callback URL configured on the External Client App; with Composio it is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add
A Salesforce org admin in the customer org who approves/installs the app and sets its policies (Permitted Users, refresh-token policy)

steps.title: Try the managed Composio connection
steps.detail: Create a Salesforce connection using Composio's managed OAUTH2 auth config (toolkit 'salesforce'). Log in to Salesforce, approve access, and run SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY once to confirm it works.

steps.title: Create an External Client App
steps.detail: In Salesforce, go to Setup, search Quick Find for 'App Manager', click App Manager, then New External Client App. Fill in the app name and your contact email. Do not try to create a legacy Connected App, since new ones are reportedly blocked as of Spring '26 (low-confidence sources).

steps.title: Enable OAuth, set callback URL and scopes
steps.detail: In the External Client App's OAuth Settings, select Enable OAuth. Enter the callback URL https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Select only the scopes 'api' and 'refresh_token'. Skip 'full' and 'web'.

links.label: Configure External Client App OAuth Settings

steps.title: Set refresh-token security policies
steps.detail: Review the refresh-token options on the app. If you enable Enforce Refresh Token IP Allowlist, add the egress IP ranges of the service that refreshes tokens, or refreshes will fail. Decide the idle refresh-token TTL (30-day option) and plan for re-authorization when tokens go idle.

steps.title: Add your Consumer Key and Secret to a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Copy the Consumer Key and Consumer Secret from the External Client App's OAuth settings. Create a custom OAUTH2 auth config for the 'salesforce' toolkit in Composio with those credentials and the scopes api and refresh_token.

steps.title: Connect an account and test both tools
steps.detail: Authorize a Salesforce user through the new auth config, then run SALESFORCE_RUN_SOQL_QUERY (a simple SELECT on Account) and SALESFORCE_CREATE_A_RECORD (a test Lead or Account). Check that refreshing the token works. A redirect_uri_mismatch error means the callback URL does not match the app's configuration.

steps.title: Org admin approves or installs the app
steps.detail: Ask a Salesforce org admin to approve or install the app and set its policies. Until they do, authorization can fail with OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC. Provider gives no duration; the wait depends on your admin.

duration.label: 15 minutes to a day (provider gives no duration)

risks.title: Legacy Connected Apps can no longer be created
risks.symptom: Old tutorials say to create a Connected App, but the option is missing or blocked in Setup.
risks.fix: Use an External Client App (Setup > App Manager > New External Client App). Reportedly Salesforce Support can re-enable Connected App creation for now, but not in future releases.

risks.title: Refresh tokens can expire or be revoked
risks.symptom: Token refresh returns HTTP 400 invalid_grant with 'expired access/refresh token'.
risks.fix: Prompt the user to re-authorize and surface a reconnect flow. Check the idle TTL and IP allowlist settings on the app. A third-party source says idle refresh tokens begin expiring on 4 November 2026, so keep integrations active.

risks.title: API limits are shared across the customer's whole org
risks.symptom: Requests fail once the org's daily API allocation is used up by your assistant plus other integrations.
risks.fix: Batch where possible, cache query results, and avoid chatty SOQL loops. Allocation is per org, not per user, and paid editions such as Enterprise start at 100,000 requests per 24 hours. Monitor usage.

risks.title: Concurrent long-running requests are capped
risks.symptom: REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED once too many requests that run 20 seconds or longer are in flight.
risks.fix: Keep SOQL queries selective and limit parallel heavy queries.

risks.title: Listing on AgentExchange/AppExchange triggers a security review
risks.symptom: Only applies if you distribute a managed package or Platform API solution through Salesforce's marketplace.
risks.fix: For your own use or direct customer connections you do not need this. If you list, plan for security review. Salesforce's own pages conflict on duration (4-6 weeks vs 4-5 weeks) and on cost ($2,700 per paid app plus $150 per year vs $999 per submission), so confirm current figures with Salesforce.

risks.title: Redirect URI mismatch
risks.fix: Make the callback URL on the External Client App exactly match the one used by Composio: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add.

risks.title: Sandbox does not receive local External Client Apps
risks.symptom: After a sandbox clone or refresh, your ECA is missing.
risks.fix: Recreate the ECA in the sandbox or package it.

risks.title: Org admin must approve the app; only five refresh tokens per user
risks.symptom: OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC during authorization, or older connections failing after a sixth authorization by the same user.
risks.fix: Ask an org admin to approve or install the app. Reuse connections instead of re-authorizing; Salesforce keeps only five active refresh tokens per user per app.

claims.text: New OAuth clients are registered as External Client Apps via Setup > App Manager > New External Client App.

sources.title: Create an External Client App in Your Org | Authorization | Salesforce DX Developer Guide | Salesforce Developers
sources.quote: From the Quick Find box in Setup, enter App Manager, then click App Manager. Click New External Client App. Update the basic information as needed, such as the external client app name and your contact email address.

verifier.note: Page gives steps: Setup > App Manager > New External Client App.

claims.text: After selecting Enable OAuth on the external client app you enter a callback URL that Salesforce redirects to during OAuth.

sources.title: Configure the External Client App OAuth Settings | Salesforce Help
sources.quote: In the OAuth Settings area of the page, select Enable OAuth. The OAuth Settings area expands and the OAuth settings fields are visible. Enter the callback URL (endpoint) that Salesforce calls back to your application during OAuth.

verifier.note: cited quote not found on the fetched page

claims.text: New legacy Connected Apps can no longer be created as of Spring '26 unless Salesforce Support enables it, and Support will not be able to in future releases.

sources.title: Salesforce Platform: New Connected Apps Can No Longer Be Created in Spring '26 | Salesforce Help
sources.quote: However, no new connected apps can be created with the Spring ‘26 release unless enabled by Salesforce Support. In future releases, Salesforce Support won’t be able to enable the creation of new connected apps.

claims.text: OAuth scopes are selected on the external client app and are granted as tokens after the app is authorized.

sources.title: Configure the External Client App OAuth Settings | Salesforce Help
sources.quote: Select the OAuth scopes to apply to the external client app. OAuth scopes define permissions for the external client app, which are granted as tokens after the app is authorized.

claims.text: Salesforce's Mobile SDK docs say that for most apps the refresh_token, web and api scopes are sufficient.

sources.title: Scope Parameter Values | Authentication, Security, and Identity in Mobile Apps | Mobile SDK Development Guide | Salesforce Developers
sources.quote: For most apps, refresh_token, web, and api are sufficient.

claims.text: AppExchange security review guidance says apps should apply least privilege to scopes and must not rely on device, implicit or username/password flows.

sources.title: Connected Apps (CAs) and External Client Apps (ECAs) AppExchange Security Review Submission Guidance | Salesforce Help
sources.quote: Apps must not rely on these OAuth flows: device flow; implicit grant flow; username/password flow (retiring in Winter '27). Apply the principle of least privilege when using scopes.

verifier.note: cited quote not found on the fetched page

claims.text: The Enforce Refresh Token IP Allowlist option on an external client app restricts which IPs can complete the web server or refresh token flow.

sources.title: Configure the External Client App OAuth Settings | Salesforce Help
sources.quote: When you turn on Enforce Refresh Token IP Allowlist, only IPs in allowed ranges can complete the OAuth web server flow or the refresh token flow.

verifier.note: cited quote not found on the fetched page

claims.text: Distributing managed packages or Platform API solutions on AgentExchange requires passing Salesforce's security review.

sources.title: How the AgentExchange Security Review Works | ISVforce Guide: Build and Distribute AgentExchange Solutions | ISVforce Guide | Salesforce Developers

verifier.note: Page states these solutions must pass security review to be distributed on AgentExchange.

claims.text: Salesforce says security review time frames are estimates and depend on submission completeness and volume. Salesforce pages disagree on the total: the partner page says about 4-6 weeks from a complete submission, the Trailhead page says typically 4-5 weeks. The packaging guide breaks it into 1-2 weeks verification, 3-4 weeks first test, 2-3 weeks resubmission.
